checkpoints.description: [1/2] plan: inline a literal-token arg_byte fast path at the call site (rip-relative len + pointer loads from the static argv cache, SIB movzx through [ptr_home+idx_home] for register homes, negative/downed bounds branch and a miss route to the runtime helper) so argv_walk stops paying call+ret plus 12 helper instructions per byte; contract: arg_byte answers -1 for negative token or index, at or past the token length, or for an unadjusted cache - those cases keep the helper; dependency: reintroduces mov_load_rip/cmp_load_rip/mov_store_rip in cairn/machine.py as failed-call-site primitives (ADR-058 lesson: carry a 3-way same-window A/B early, reject fast if lossy); concurrency: none, codegen emissions are single-threaded; state: argv cache flag/count/table layout untouched, no new data labels

impact_assessment.why: contract: arg_byte(-1 wrapper) semantics must hold for every token/index pair including negative and out-of-range; dependency: the ADR-058 measurement says inlining can lose to a call on this machine, so the plan ships with an early 3-way same-window A/B gate; concurrency: none, single-threaded emission; state: no change to the argv cache layout or runtime reserves
impact_assessment.benefits: contract: keeps every arg_byte guarantee while closing the 32.6 vs 20.2 ms gap to C's argv_walk twin; dependency: reuses the existing str_byte inline machinery (nonnegative_slots, movzx_load8_sib) instead of new lowering; concurrency: no risk; state: no migration

impact_assessment.mitigation: contract: failing-first tests pin the -1 branches for negative index, past-end index and the negative-token case alongside the fast path; dependency: 3-way same-window A/B (old, runtime-only, inline) before any commit, revert on first negative delta; concurrency: no threads; state: no on-disk or runtime format change
